issues.title: Canonical foundation wrapper's fixed inner 120s timeout
issues.classification: actual marginal timing, not a semantic assertion failure
issues.rootCause: subprocess.TimeoutExpired propagates past the report write, so the launcher has NO failure path: the previous run's PASS report survives as the file on disk and only the exit code and a traceback signal failure.

correction.budgetForm: module constant, deliberately not a flag or environment variable
correction.budgetRationale: slowest child measured 122.3s here and 121.3s at root; 600s is ~5x observed cost, suite bounded at 5x600s
timeoutReportBehaviour: same shape, same five entries, loop continues past a timeout
timedOut boolean present on EVERY entry (uniform, not conditional)
reportSha256 null: a run that did not finish must not claim a child report it did not write
explicit 'TIMEOUT: no result after 600s' marker on stderr
correction.decodeFix: TimeoutExpired.stdout/.stderr are bytes even under text=True (verified empirically); writing them raw would raise TypeError from json.dumps and skip the report write again
notDone: no pin check disabled or weakened
pin-before-execution unchanged; the failures branch is byte-identical

rejectedAlternatives.reason: band-aid: no failure path, stale-PASS hazard survives and merely becomes rarer

rejectedAlternatives.option: catch the timeout and abort the loop

rejectedAlternatives.reason: child reports are deterministic (identity-report.json byte-identical across runs), so after==before on a SUCCESSFUL run and the field would read false for a child that did write

issues.title: verify_scope_parameter_binding at-most-one ordering is unheld by any control
issues.gap: both existing ordering controls supply one of the two candidates; for a candidate the payload match SUCCEEDS, so the ambiguity is reached and refused under either ordering and neither control holds the position
controlProperties: real existing fixtures/rows plus one distinct third scope document
third document admitted through the owning unit's pinned validator, not merely asserted
actual error_code/detail pairs on real Refusal objects and a real returned digest
distinguishes at-most-one precedence from missing, from ordinary mismatch, and from valid selection

commentCorrection.falseClaim: checking the digest first would let a caller holding one of two candidate documents obtain a verified digest
commentCorrection.whyFalse: with the guard below the match, a candidate's document matches its row, the match falls through without returning, and the ambiguity is still reached and still refuses; nobody obtains a verified digest
commentCorrection.actualConsequence: the answer given to a caller holding NEITHER candidate changes from CONFIG.INVALID to BASELINE.SCOPE_PARAMETER_DIGEST_MISMATCH, reporting a defect of the SPEC ALONE as a statement about the supplied document
commentCorrection.scope: comment only; executable ordering and public routes untouched
commentCorrection.deliberatelyUnchanged: the docstring's 'refused before any payload comparison' rationale is about why the guard EXISTS (removing it entirely WOULD yield a verified digest) and is accurate; flagged as easy to misread, left to the integrator

mutationDemonstration.mutation: at-most-one guard block moved verbatim below the payload-match block
